explanation: An if statement runs a branch when its condition compares unequal to zero. An else branch handles the remaining case. Logical operators can combine smaller tests.
exampleExplanation: Both comparisons must be true for the branch to execute.
misconceptions: A comparison such as 0 <= score <= 10 does not test a range as it does in algebra.
A semicolon immediately after an if condition creates an empty controlled statement.

reference.title: Local C reference on logical tests
reference.text: The && operator stops when its left operand is false. The || operator stops when its left operand is true. Use braces to show which statements belong to each branch.
